column5: The Virginia Family's Guide to Special Education we worked from is the May 2023 edition. Is that still the current version? (N = it has been replaced; please give the new title or date in a comment.)

The Virginia Procedural Safeguards Notice we worked from is the "Revised September 2024" edition (form SS/SE-4 (1/25)). Is that still the current version? (N = it has been replaced; please give the new date in a comment.)

Our list shows "Level I services" as services delivered for less than half the school day and "Level II services" as half the school day or more. We wrote those thresholds from memory and have not confirmed them. Are they right? (N = wrong; please explain.)

Our list says Virginia separates three things: "home-based instruction" (an IEP placement), "homebound instruction" (for a medical confinement), and "home instruction" or "home tutoring" (parent-chosen alternatives to school). Is that how the terms are used? (N = no; please explain.)

Our list records the "Modified Standard Diploma" as discontinued, but still found in older records, and the "Applied Studies Diploma" as the diploma earned by completing IEP requirements. We could not open VDOE's own fact sheets for these, and the September 2024 notice names only the standard and advanced studies diplomas. Is that accurate? (N = wrong or out of date; please explain.)

Our list has "campus-based student support team" with "school-based team" and "child study" as other names for it. Which of these do Northern Virginia school divisions actually say? (N = none of them, or the real name is different; please give it in a comment.)

We know "Special Permission Locally Awarded Verified Credit" (SPLAVC, also "SPLAVC-A") only from the title and scope of an August 2024 VDOE fact sheet. Is that the right name, and is it used in IEP meetings? (N = wrong or not used; please explain.)

Differences between school divisions in Northern Virginia (for example Fairfax, Arlington, Loudoun, Prince William, Alexandria or Falls Church): names for forms, teams, meetings or programs that one division says and another does not.
Statewide tests and alternate assessments: which names appear on Virginia IEPs today? (Our list has SOL, VAAP and the Virginia Essentialized Standards of Learning.)

Diplomas and other completion documents: which ones appear on Virginia IEPs and transition plans today? (Our list has Standard, Advanced Studies, Applied Studies and the discontinued Modified Standard diploma, a Certificate of Program Completion and the GED.)
